evidence.claim: Open Library record: A Treatise on the Method of Least Squares, first publication year 1868, Trubner; a later 1879 Lippincott edition has the same title.

milestones.note: Gauss's Theoria combinationis (1823) is an earlier systematic treatment of least squares that was not checked, so this may be contested. Merriman's Elements (Open Library 1877) is a later textbook.

notes: Sources: MacTutor Legendre, Gauss, Laplace; Wikipedia Least squares; archive.org; Crossref (Stigler 1981). The priority dispute is the central uncertainty: Legendre published first (1805), Gauss claimed 1795. Wikipedia credits the first clear exposition to Legendre, which fits MacTutor. No separate naming or institution milestone was found; the term 'higher arithmetic' is Gauss's own, per Wikipedia. person without verified work: Adrien-Marie Legendre (developer). person without verified work: Leonhard Euler (systematiser). person without verified work: Joseph-Louis Lagrange (systematiser). Added in thin-3 pass: Kummer 1847, Dirichlet-Dedekind 1863, Legendre's work citation. Euler and Lagrange were dropped from people because no verified work could be attached (the earlier entries had none); their results are the background Wikipedia describes. MacTutor Gauss confirms the 17-gon appears as Section VII and the 1801 publication. The dual role of the 1801 book is noted on both milestones.
